assertionIntent: Prevents port collisions, prevents publishing a test broker on every host interface, and prevents a run starting against a service that is up but not usable.
behaviorContract: Every published port is written as 127.0.0.1::<container port> so Docker assigns a free loopback port per run and publishes it atomically; the runner asks Docker afterwards which ports were bound. Every healthcheck asserts usable service, not a started process: RabbitMQ checks running plus port connectivity because the setup creates the test vhost over HTTP; ActiveMQ checks that Jolokia answers with status 200; SQL Server runs SELECT 1; PostgreSQL runs pg_isready; Artemis dials its own container name because the acceptor does not bind loopback; the HAProxy check deliberately only proves it is listening, because whether anything is behind it is what the outage changes.
discoveredCase: Host ports are ephemeral and bound to loopback; readiness means the service answers
notes: Successor: Testcontainers wait strategies. Each of the six readiness definitions is a separate promise; a generic port-open wait is weaker than five of them. PostgreSQL keeps its data directory in tmpfs so no stale volume can survive with an earlier run's credentials. The ActiveMQ image carries exactly one delta against the official configuration, schedulerSupport=true, which DelayRetry_Specs needs; groups.properties binds vicione_ci to the admins role so the run account is not refused with HTTP 403.

behaviorContract: An SNS subscription FILTER POLICY on the queue's subscription routes each message only to the queue whose policy matches its RoutingKey message attribute.
boundaries: Two mutually exclusive filter policies over one topic.
discoveredCase: Two runtime-connected queues 'TestCase-R-foo' and 'TestCase-R-bar', each subscribed to the Message topic with QueueSubscriptionAttributes['FilterPolicy'] = {"RoutingKey": ["<key>"]}; two messages published with different RoutingKey headers
negativeAndFailurePaths: The negative - foo must NOT reach the bar queue - is the entire point and it is unobservable in this design.
notes: LocalIntegration: LocalStack (tests/.../docker-compose.yml, localstack/localstack:3.0.2) implements the SQS and SNS data plane this case uses; the baseline already targets it through the product's LocalstackHost() helper. Two further defects: the two HostReceiveEndpointHandle values are returned and never stopped (leaked endpoints, non-awaited cleanup), and the queue names are fixed, not run-unique, so two concurrent runs share them. Flag also for C4b: SNS filter-policy evaluation semantics (numeric, prefix, anything-but operators) are an AWS engine behaviour LocalStack only approximates.

assertionIntent: TestHandler.Count is 0 once the Fault<TestCommand> arrives.
behaviorContract: The in-memory outbox suppresses the inner message on every failed attempt including the delayed redelivery, so a consumer that always throws never delivers its inner message.
boundaries: Retry then delayed redelivery then fault; on SQS delayed redelivery uses DelaySeconds, whose minimum granularity is 1 second while the configured interval is 100ms - the configuration and the transport disagree.
discoveredCase: UseDelayedRedelivery(1x100ms) + UseMessageRetry(1x100ms) + UseInMemoryOutbox (message-type scoped filters, consumer publishes InnerCommand); the consumer produces an inner message and then throws
negativeAndFailurePaths: Count must be 0.
notes: LocalIntegration: LocalStack (tests/.../docker-compose.yml, localstack/localstack:3.0.2) implements the SQS and SNS data plane this case uses; the baseline already targets it through the product's LocalstackHost() helper. TLP-011: the inner Publish/Send is not awaited before the throw, and ++Count on a static int is not interlocked. The 100ms-vs-1s granularity mismatch is a likely root cause of the 'Flaky' marking and must be resolved, not retried away. Identical in shape to the Azure twin - three obligations duplicated per transport.

Case body inherited from FryFuture_Specs.Should_complete.
negativeAndFailurePaths: The Should_fault / Should_faulted cases are the negative paths; their bodies live in the TestFramework base classes.
notes: The configurator hard-codes SqlServerLockStatementProvider (Future_Specs.cs:21) and FutureSagaDbContextFactory hard-codes UseSqlServer, so all 16 identities are SQL-Server-only. behaviorContract: An abandoned job attempt is detected by status checks, faulted through the suspect path with no retry delay, and its late messages are suppressed on the job and job-attempt endpoints without producing a fault-of-fault.
boundaries: SuspectJobRetryCount 0 is the boundary that separates this fixture from the retried one; SuppressionCount 2 and endpoints {job, job-attempt} are exact expectations.

The job service must detect the attempt as suspect through repeated status checks, publish JobFaulted through the suspect path, and must not retry or complete it. The fixture records every suppressed message, its endpoints, the suspect fault's AttemptId, MessageId and RetryDelay, and the highest retry attempt seen.
negativeAndFailurePaths: The abandoned worker is the injected fault, and three explicit negatives are asserted: no retry, no completion, no cancellation, exactly one fault.

assertionIntent: ShouldContainSaga(Counter == 3) - the only inherited Azure.Table assertion that can detect a lost update.
behaviorContract: Concurrent updates of one Azure Table saga instance are serialised by the ETag: both increments are applied on top of each other and no update is lost.
boundaries: ConcurrentMessageLimit 16; retry 5 times at 100 ms; final Counter 3 (1 from Begin plus two increments).
discoveredCase: Begin creates the saga with Counter 1; two concurrent IncrementCounterSlowly messages each sleep 3 s inside the saga and increment. With UseMessageRetry(Interval(5,100)) resolving the ETag conflicts, the final Counter must be 3.
negativeAndFailurePaths: The concurrent update is the injected race; a lost update would leave Counter at 2.

assertionIntent: None, and that is the point: the scenario reports measurements and never a PASS. The exit code is non zero only when the scenario could not run, never because a number was worse than another number. What it looks for - a round trip that grows with the cycle count or a resource that never comes back - is a judgement a human makes from the samples.
behaviorContract: The 'bus-lifecycle' measurement: start and stop a RabbitMqTestHarness --cycles times against the pinned broker of the run, measure start, one full round trip (send plus handled) and stop separately, and every --sample-every cycles record those three durations together with ThreadPool.ThreadCount, process thread count, ThreadPool.PendingWorkItemCount and managed memory. The result is a JSON object of samples; the scenario returns numbers and passes no verdict.
boundaries: First cycle, every sample-every-th cycle and the last cycle are sampled. --sample-every greater than --cycles is refused in Program.Main because nothing between the first and the last cycle would ever be sampled. Round trip is bounded by a 30 s WaitAsync.
negativeAndFailurePaths: A start that threw still leaves a harness to dispose, which the finally block does; roundTripMilliseconds stays -1 in that case. RunScopedBroker.CreateVirtualHost throws InvalidOperationException when the runner published no host, port, user, password or management port, and the scenario refuses to start rather than measuring whatever broker is on the machine.
notes: DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY candidate 1 of exactly 2. Four independent properties justify it: (1) it needs a run-scoped pinned RabbitMQ broker and its management API and refuses to start without five published environment variables, so it is not hermetic; (2) it runs 240 bus start/stop cycles, i.e. minutes, so it cannot sit in a profile that must run complete on every change; (3) it produces no verdict at all, so a PASS would be a claim it does not make; (4) tools/diagnostics/.../README.md states it explicitly: 'Two scenarios that are started deliberately and gate nothing' and 'The measurements themselves stay on demand and gate nothing.' Its hermetically testable seams are already carved out and are covered by the 44 anchor identities.

behaviorContract: The 'publish-load' measurement: publish --messages messages concurrently to one auto-delete, non-durable endpoint on the pinned broker with publisher confirmation deliberately off, wait until every identity of the run has been seen at least once, then observe for a further DrainWindow (3 s), then stop the bus inside QuiescenceBudget (30 s), then read the ledger.
